title: The Garden Party
focus: a girl's first encounter with death across the class line

teacherSummary.text: The wealthy Sheridans prepare a garden party. Laura learns that a young carter from the poor cottages below, Scott, has been killed, and wants to cancel; her mother and sister refuse. After the party, Laura takes a basket of leftovers to the widow and is led to see the dead man, who looks peaceful and beautiful. She apologizes for her hat and, sobbing, tries to tell her brother Laurie what life is.

segments.activity: Model the close reading of the anchor quotation using the written think-aloud below.
segments.script: First, meaning. I read “You are being very absurd, Laura” slowly and put it in my own words: Laura wants to cancel the party because a workman nearby has died, and her sister tells her she is being absurd. Next, craft. I notice the word is said calmly, as if the matter is obvious. The strongest word is “absurd”: it dismisses her empathy as silly, which is how the wealthy family protects its comfort. Then, effect. Why does Laura's family call her "absurd"? My answer: The family thinks feeling for a poor neighbor is unreasonable; the line shows the class blindness Laura is just starting to see.
